extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED/USPTO staff and counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing an affidavit of resignation submitted to the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline to obtain exclusion on consent from practice before the Office. Covers required affidavit acknowledgements, applicable regulatory provisions, and post-order obligations (publication, compliance for reinstatement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary and uncoerced consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's consent must be freely and voluntarily rendered, and the respondent must not be subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit of Resignation should explicitly state that consent is given freely and voluntarily (item 1 of the Affidavit). The Director reviews this as part of compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and alleged misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge awareness that a disciplinary complaint is pending and summarize the allegations (including criminal charges, guilty pleas, and factual allegations underlying the complaint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should state awareness of the specific proceeding number and describe the nature of allegations (e.g., conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering, statements about the scheme and amounts involved), and note any failure to respond to OED requests (item 2(a)-(d)). This factual acknowledgment informs the Director's review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific factual allegations regarding conduct (scheme, convictions, non-response to OED)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit may set out particulars: e.g., conspiracy with another practitioner to route work/payments, defrauding a client of a stated amount, guilty pleas to named federal statutes, and failure to respond to OED's Request for Information or to report convictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including concrete factual allegations in the affidavit (as here: scheme to defraud $2.4 million; guilty pleas to 18 U.S.C. §1349 and §1956(h); not responding to OED) supports the Office's determination and the later presumption for reinstatement review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of alleged regulatory violations (USPTO Code provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit should acknowledge the disciplinary complaint alleges violations of specified provisions of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), 10.23(b)(4), 10.23(c)(2)(i), 10.84(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document lists the particular provisions alleged to have been violated. Even if the respondent does not admit violation, acknowledging the allegations and the cited provisions is part of the resignation/consent package the Director reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of alleged regulatory violations (USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit should acknowledge alleged violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.801(b), 11.804(b), 11.804(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing the specific Rules of Professional Conduct that the complaint alleges were violated provides notice and grounds for exclusion on consent and future reinstatement presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-admission coupled with reinstatement presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not admit violating disciplinary rules in the pending complaint but must acknowledge that, upon any future reinstatement application, the OED Director will conclusively presume for reinstatement purposes that the allegations are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit language reflecting this limited but conclusive presumption (item 4) is required/accepted as part of the affidavit of resignation process under § 11.27 and affects how future reinstatement applications are evaluated under §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and understanding of applicable regulations and legal consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must state that he has fully read and understands the relevant regulations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60) and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit acknowledgment of having read and understood these sections (item 5) demonstrates informed consent and is considered by the Director when approving the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must expressly consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters as the remedy under the affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear statement of consent to exclusion (item 6) is required; approval of the affidavit results in an Order excluding the respondent on consent effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to approve affidavit and impose exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has authority pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and exclude a respondent on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites statutory and regulatory authority as the legal basis for approving the affidavit and entering the exclusion on consent; practitioners should understand this statutory/regulatory framework when submitting or reviewing such affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must 'comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)'
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit submitted for exclusion on consent must meet the specific requirements set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a),' triggering approval. Parties preparing an affidavit should review §11.27(a) to ensure all mandatory elements are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires electronic publication at http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp and an Official Gazette notice containing specific material (summary of allegations, cited rules, statement regarding reinstatement presumptions). The template text in the Order demonstrates the content expected in the Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-exclusion obligations: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order expressly requires compliance with §11.58 (which governs record-keeping and related obligations after suspension/exclusion). Those excluded must follow the duties set out in that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and obligations: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit and Final Order emphasize that reinstatement will be governed by §11.60 and that the OED Director will apply the conclusive presumption described in the affidavit when evaluating any future reinstatement application.
